title: Voronoi Diagram-based Multiple Power Plane Generation on Redistribution Layers in 3D ICs
problem: Power and ground plane generation for multiple power supplies on redistribution layers in 3D ICs is currently a manual and time-consuming task. Existing methods struggle to efficiently optimize more than ten power supplies simultaneously on limited RDLs while respecting signal routing constraints and design rules.
motivation: Optimized power plane generation on redistribution layers is critical for achieving high-performance 3D computing systems with proper inter-chip connectivity and power integrity.
method: The paper proposes a Voronoi diagram-based methodology that partitions redistribution layer space to simultaneously optimize power/ground planes for all supply nets. The approach utilizes available white space while accounting for signal routing blockages, power integrity constraints, and complex design rules to determine optimal plane regions.
key_novelty: Using Voronoi diagrams to automatically and simultaneously optimize multiple power/ground planes on redistribution layers, enabling design automation for a previously manual process.
contributions: Novel Voronoi diagram-based framework for multi-supply power/ground plane generation
Simultaneous optimization of all power/ground nets achieving optimal area utilization
Integrated consideration of signal routing blockages and complex design rules
Improved cross-layer power integrity through minimized redundant vias
limitations: Specific limitations of the approach and detailed comparisons with prior methods are not discussed in the abstract.
primary_theme: Automated power plane generation for 3D chiplet interconnection layers
